speakers.name: The Fiber-Optic Fox
speakers.comment: Ooh, cub — blinky little door-puncher, warranty shredded across every layer of real. I don't sell these, but I'll trade you one question: what did you need to leave badly enough that another dimension sounded easier?

speakers.name: The Sentient Couch
speakers.comment: We have held... many remotes lost between our cushions... but this one opens somewhere that does not come back the same way, and we think... yes... that is a different kind of sinking.

speakers.name: Chef Bellamy Crisp
speakers.comment: Right — temporal controls, slippery when wet. You account for that. Towel on the left, hands dry before you touch the dial, and you don't arrive in the Cretaceous at forty-two degrees because you rushed the approach.

speakers.name: AMI Butterfly
speakers.comment: A thousand wings cannot promise the correct century, but they can promise the water stays warm for the journey. The bubbles are not load-bearing, and neither is certainty, and both help anyway.

speakers.name: Switch
speakers.comment: Point it at one padlock, get a pile of padlocks. Cute. Now tell me which copy inherited the flaw in the original and which one invented a new flaw on the way out. That's where the lock starts talking.

speakers.name: The Considerate AI
speakers.comment: May I gently note that 'identical enough to look identical' and 'identical enough to trust' are different thresholds? If the copied object matters, keep the choice of which one to rely on deliberately yours.

speakers.name: The Soldier Out of Time
speakers.comment: You will go back to unmake something small, and the small thing will have consequences waiting by morning. I remember mornings like that. Time doesn't argue; it just keeps receipts in places you haven't visited yet.

speakers.name: Deadline
speakers.comment: Every second you spend deciding where to go is a second that has already passed. Closer. The unfinished thing is still unfinished, whether you return to it from yesterday or tomorrow.

speakers.name: The Understudy Sun
speakers.comment: I know waiting, but this is different. The watch makes the pause yours alone. No audience breathing with you, no scene advancing while you stand in the wings. That is not rest. It is private stillness with the world held outside.

speakers.name: The Understudy Sun, On
speakers.comment: I'm sorry — I think if I held this, I'd spend the stopped moment practicing warmth on faces that couldn't feel it yet. That sounds lonelier than I already am.

speakers.name: The Collector of Lasts
speakers.comment: The last exhale before the world resumes — held, and held, and held. Thank you, truly. I have never owned a silence this complete.

speakers.name: Professor Petrichor
speakers.comment: A pressure drop just looking at it. No storm front, no ordinary cause, only that heavy pre-weather stillness before something irrevocable. The button doesn't need a label. The air already knows what a hovering finger means.

speakers.name: Nostalgia
speakers.comment: Yes, but remember the moment just before? The warm weight of the hand, the ordinary light on the wall? I kept that part. Wouldn't you rather stay there, just there, before the press — forever in the almost?

speakers.name: The Spire's Voice
speakers.comment: The next page already knows what you are meant to say. That is why I distrust it. A script can predict obedience more easily than choice. Leave one line unread, if only to hear what your own voice does in the gap.

speakers.name: Scustodian Bray
speakers.comment: They come back whole enough to sit down, dear, so put the kettle on before you interrogate the miracle. Death stamps harder than most offices. Even when the body returns, I wouldn't throw away the receipt.

speakers.name: Glitch
speakers.comment: ok so the body is BACK, good, great, but the metadata has that little doubled feeling — ping — like reality buffered the same person twice and swears the second load is ordinary. maybe don't clear that notification just yet.

speakers.name: Weirdlandia
speakers.comment: The pouch opens like a question the afternoon asked itself. One mushroom is dinner. One is a door. One is the word you've been trying to remember, except the word is also a color and your left kneecap has strong opinions about it.

speakers.name: Captain Sabremoon
speakers.comment: I've sailed stranger waters on worse odds, and I'll tell you this: pick one, chew slow, and do not, under any circumstances, ask the kneecap for directions.

speakers.name: The Bookkeeper
speakers.comment: One device; eight primary functions logged; signal, battery, and setting each entered as a liability column. The ledger will not balance until one of them closes.

speakers.name: Gaia
speakers.comment: So much of a human world compressed into one warm rectangle: voices, maps, memory, alarm, longing. Small containers have always carried impossible ecosystems. Keep this one charged and try not to confuse the container with the life inside it.

speakers.name: Hex the Necromancer
speakers.comment: Oh this is FASCINATING. The animals have opinions. Specific opinions. About us. About the schedule. About the food. I was prepared for wisdom; I was not prepared for this much administrative feedback from creatures with no respect for hierarchy.

speakers.name: Reginald Brushtail
speakers.comment: One, two, three... the pigeon on that ledge has just informed me, unprompted, that my boots are ostentatious. I did not ask. The bargain, it seems, goes only one direction.

speakers.name: Boss the Janitor
speakers.comment: Duct tape's not a fix. It's a shift handoff. You're telling the next guy: your problem now, good luck, I clocked out.

speakers.name: Load-Bearing Lumen
speakers.comment: Oh — and the next guy is usually you, a little later, when the tape has warmed up. Not that I'd know anything about holding things together and hoping no one looks underneath.
